findings.description: Critical: Expired-lease takeover is conditioned on the absence of contradictory live-process evidence, but the plan never defines what process identity is recorded, where that record lives, how PID reuse or host identity is handled, or how the takeover checker distinguishes a live old writer from stale process metadata. The registry schema has no process token, and the only related statement says the controller persists unspecified non-authoritative process context. Implementers must therefore either fail every expired takeover as indeterminate or silently omit the zombie check that the fencing model relies on.
findings.resolution: Define a concrete, local-first process-evidence contract (storage path/schema, PID plus process-start/host identity, writer and cleanup ownership, atomic ordering relative to lease acquire/release, stale-record rules, and takeover outcomes) and add process-level fixtures for live zombie, PID reuse, missing evidence, stale evidence, and cross-host/indeterminate cases. If reliable evidence cannot be obtained, make quarantine the explicit deterministic fallback rather than claiming clean takeover.

findings.description: Critical: The spec requires a changed head SHA to invalidate an operator delivery-stage disposition, but the durable operatorOverride contract stores only actor, selected_stage, reason, and recorded_at. It does not bind the override to the base/head SHAs or a classification digest. After an ambiguous PR is overridden as proposal, new code can be pushed while the persisted override still selects planning-only validation and preserve-active-change cleanup, and the executor has no durable value against which to detect staleness.
findings.resolution: Add the exact base_sha and head_sha (and preferably ruleset/classification digest) that the operator inspected to operatorOverride, require execution to compare them with the refreshed classification before honoring the override, and force the node back to blocked when either SHA changes. Add schema fixtures and resume/execution tests for stale overrides.

findings.description: Critical: lease release-owner clears every exact-owner lease without the quarantine rule applied to release-session or unsafe per-entry release. A recovery operator can therefore clear a live or crashed owner's bulk leases while preserved dirty/non-durable worktrees remain recovery_required=false, making them ordinary-acquire eligible and reopening both concurrent-writer and silent-dirty-state adoption risks.
findings.resolution: Make release-owner non-destructive but quarantine every still-present matching checkout before clearing ownership, unless it performs the same owner-fenced clean/durable disposal transaction as explicit finalization. Return quarantined_count and per-entry outcomes, and add tests showing a bulk recovery release cannot make preserved state ordinarily adoptable.

findings.description: Nit: Package worktrees are required to be disposed after integration only when remotely durable, but the plan never states which remote ref proves durability for a child branch or when the parent feature branch must be pushed relative to child disposal. Existing package branches are local integration children and are not necessarily pushed under their own names, so checking each entry's branch would quarantine successful packages even when their commits are reachable from the pushed parent feature branch.
findings.resolution: Specify that package HEAD durability is proven against the pushed parent feature ref after integration (or require child branches to be pushed explicitly), persist/pass that expected ref to teardown, and add a fixture where an unpushed child ref is safely removed because its exact HEAD is reachable from the pushed parent ref.

findings.description: Nit: Holding the registry lock across Git removal and registry deletion prevents concurrent acquisition but does not make the two side effects atomic. A crash after git worktree remove succeeds and before the registry entry is deleted leaves a live leased orphan entry; the contract defines idempotency only when both the entry and checkout are absent and does not specify owner-fenced reconciliation for this one-sided state.
findings.resolution: Define repeated teardown of a missing checkout with a still-present exact owner/lease registry entry to remove or tombstone the entry safely, and define release-session behavior for the same state. Add fault-injection tests at the boundary after Git removal and before registry replacement so restart cannot leave a live blocker until TTL expiry.

findings.description: Nit: recovery adopt says it atomically acquires a manual lease but does not define the resulting session_id, phase, TTL/timestamps, recovery reason clearing, exit codes, or JSON output, even though every one of those fields is mandatory or operationally relevant in schema v2. The safety-critical adoption path is therefore less specified than ordinary acquire.
findings.resolution: Define recovery adopt as a complete field-by-field transition, include required machine-readable output and conflict/inspection-failure exits, and add schema-valid fixtures for successful adoption plus dirty, missing, and concurrent-owner failures.

findings.description: The revised plan correctly separates retention, activity, and recovery quarantine, and it carries one acquisition-specific lease id through mutation boundaries so same-owner resumes cannot revive an expired writer.
findings.resolution: Preserve these state boundaries and fencing assertions during implementation.

findings.description: The delivery classifier fails closed on incomplete primary evidence and conflicting markers, while author-vendor claims remain unverified routing evidence rather than authentication; these are sound safety boundaries.
findings.resolution: Retain the conservative ambiguity and reviewer-routing behavior in implementation tests.
